subject: bauhausBird
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: songbird on a branch.
Style: Bauhaus primary-colour geometry.
reasoning:
I'm planning a Bauhaus-style songbird perched on a branch, with a skeletal rest pose including separate upper/lower beak joints and named parts for both the bird and the branch, aiming for a moderately rich design around a few hundred parts.

Color scheme: a blue egg-shaped body with a cream belly, red triangular-patterned wing, a yellow-and-black block-fan tail, a yellow spherical head with a concentric black/white/red eye, black geometric beak cones, and thin black rod legs gripping a black branch decorated with colorful geometric "leaf" shapes (red squares, yellow circles, blue triangles).

Sizing it at roughly 0.15 m long, perched at about 0.13 m tall, with the branch as the lowest element resting near y=0.012 and spanning about 0.4 m along the X axis so the whole model sits properly on the ground plane.

Now I'm planning the skeleton: a hips root joint, then chains for spine, neck, head with a separate jaw for the beak, a tail chain, wing chains per side (shoulder-elbow-wrist-tip), and leg chains with toe digits, making sure each chain correctly references its parent joint so only the hips joint has no parent. I'm also working out the bird's tilted perched posture, angling the body axis roughly 30-40 degrees from horizontal to look natural on the branch.

Setting coordinates for the branch, body, legs, and hips so the proportions read as a chunky stylized songbird roughly 0.17m tall while perched, with feet gripping the branch top and the hip joint positioned just above the branch surface.

Thinking through the spine chain next: a short catmull path from hips through the chest, with two named joints marking the spine1 and spine2 positions, keeping the hips as the root joint that the spine parents from.

Now I'm planning the neck chain, running from the top of the spine up to the base of the head with a short curved path of named joints, parented to the second spine joint.

For the head itself, I'm working out where to center it in model space relative to the neck and body, forward-facing, sized roughly 0.04 in radius, so the skull sits naturally atop the neck.

Now I'm lofting the body along the spine, defining a series of stations from hips through spine to neck with varying width and height at each point to shape the torso, and figuring out how the bone/chain binding and section orientation should work for smooth interpolation between stations.

Smooth skin via sweep seems nicer, so I'll define the bone list as spine and neck, letting the spine chain own the rear region by positioning its joints to overlap the hips area, while keeping the body path spanning the full torso length. I'm weighing whether to include hips explicitly in the bone list or let the spine's starting joint absorb that region.

For coloring, I'm sketching a Bauhaus-inspired bold geometric paint scheme: a sharp (non-gradient) split between a blue back and cream-white belly based on normal direction, with a possible accent band and a red circle placed on the chest using position-based masks.

Finding the right surface point for the chest roundel...

Now thinking about wing construction: Bauhaus-style wings built from joint chains (shoulder, elbow, wrist) with flight feathers as fanned extruded shapes in primary colors with black stripes, considering the folded versus extended pose.

For pose, I'm weighing a T-pose-like spread wings against a natural perched look — I'll settle on wings held out at a moderate angle (around 50°), drooping slightly down-back and clearly separated from the body, balancing anatomical clarity with a readable songbird silhouette.

Defining the wing joint chains...

For feathers, I'm planning a thin tapered arm sweep in red, plus a fan of extruded primary feather blades at the wrist with squared or semi-circle Bauhaus-style ends and alternating colors, along with secondary feathers along the forearm.

Positioning feathers along each wing, sweeping them backward and outward with angles increasing toward the body, and scaling lengths so outer feathers are longer than inner ones.

I'll scale toward eagle-ish proportions, arm length going from 0.04 at the shoulder to 0.14 at the tip, with feathers around 0.07 long for a total span near 0.3. For anchoring feathers to the skeleton, I'll pass the chain point's frame directly as the `at` argument so it carries bone data for rigid attachment.

For extra Bauhaus detail, I'm considering adding small contrasting discs at some feather tips and triangular prism shapes (using low-segment cylinders) as wing coverts laid along the arm, building outline helpers for these shapes to keep the part count reasonable.

Now I'm sketching the tail as a fan of five flat rectangular blades spreading out and slightly down from the tail base, colored in alternating red, yellow, black, and blue, with a short tail bone chain (tail1-tail3) for the feathers to attach to and angle outward from.

The exact sign doesn't matter for the blade's thickness direction. For the head, I'm planning a low-poly yellow sphere with painted color zones -- maybe black for a crown marking and splitting by vertical position to suggest facial features in a simplified Bauhaus style.

For eyes, I'm thinking of using decal-style concentric roundels: black ring, white band, colored inner circle, and black pupil, keeping with the geometric Bauhaus aesthetic.

I'll place them at ±60° azimuth, 15° elevation on the sides of the head so they read well from the front for a songbird-like cute look, mirrored symmetrically since the design itself is symmetric. For the beak, I'm planning a simple 4-sided pyramid/cone shape for the upper mandible to keep the geometric faceted style consistent.

Working out beak colors and wedge shape...

Still shaping the beak geometry...

Writing beak sweep geometry...

For the jaw, I'm placing the joint off the head position aimed forward, with the lower beak sweeping from near the head down to a lower tip point, positioned slightly below and offset from the upper beak so they don't perfectly overlap but form a believable gap for the mouth line.

Now I'm skipping nostril details and moving to the crest — planning three Bauhaus-style triangular blades standing up along the crown of the head, each a different height and color (red, blue, yellow), tilted back and arranged in a row to form a stylized crest.

Head gets a black cap with yellow underneath, crest in red/blue/red. I'm adding small red cylinder discs flush against the cheeks below the eyes as cheek markings, placed via surface-hit positioning. I'll bend the hock backward with a simple three-point chain (hip, hock, ankle) per side, naming joints with L/R suffixes based on sign of the X coordinate. For toes, I'm planning three forward digits plus one back hind toe wrapping the branch, each as a short two-joint chain for simplicity.
